title: "Scenario catalogue"

```{r}
#| include: false
source("_common.R")

# one record per scenario, read from the module's own library, so this page
# always matches the scenarios that ship with the module
design_names <- c(cross_sectional = "Cross-sectional", cohort = "Cohort", case_control = "Case-control",
                  matched_cc = "Matched case-control", nested_cc = "Nested case-control", case_cohort = "Case-cohort",
                  ecological = "Ecological", rct = "Randomised trial", cluster_rct = "Cluster trial",
                  factorial = "2x2 factorial", crossover = "Crossover", longitudinal = "Longitudinal trial",
                  prognosis = "Prognosis", diagnostic = "Diagnostic accuracy")
type_names <- c(binary = "binary", event = "time to event", continuous = "continuous", count = "count")
recs <- lapply(names(lib$scenarios), function(id) {
    raw <- lib$scenarios[[id]]
    sc <- load_scenario(lib, id)
    des <- unique(unlist(lapply(names(sc$outcomes), function(o) compatible_designs(sc, o))))
    refs <- unlist(raw$references)
    data <- grep("^Data:", refs, value = TRUE)
    feats <- c(
        if (length(sc$interventions)) "intervention",
        if (any(vapply(sc$outcomes, function(o) !is.null(o$competing), TRUE))) "competing risks",
        if (any(vapply(sc$outcomes, function(o) length(o$markers) > 0, TRUE))) "diagnostic markers",
        if (any(vapply(sc$outcomes, function(o) any(vapply(o$effects, function(e) !is.null(e$by), TRUE)), TRUE))) "effect modification",
        if (length(sc$rule_order)) "rules",
        if (length(sc$null_variables)) "null variables",
        if (nrow(sc$edges)) "causal structure")
    list(id = id,
         label = tr_text(raw$label, "en"),
         domain = tools::toTitleCase(raw$domain %||% ""),
         population = tr_text(raw$population, "en"),
         outcomes = unname(lapply(sc$outcomes, function(o) list(label = tr_text(o$label, "en"), type = type_names[[o$type]]))),
         types = unique(unname(vapply(sc$outcomes, function(o) type_names[[o$type]], ""))),
         designs = unname(design_names[des]),
         source = if (length(data)) "open data" else "published study",
         dataset = if (length(data)) sub("^Data: *", "", data[1]) else "",
         nvars = length(sc$variables),
         features = feats,
         references = setdiff(refs, data),
         teaching = gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(tr_text(raw$teaching, "en"))))
})
n_open <- sum(vapply(recs, function(r) r$source == "open data", TRUE))
json <- jsonlite::toJSON(recs, auto_unbox = TRUE)
```

The module ships with **`r length(recs)` scenarios**, one clinical question
each. Most replicate a real study: `r n_open` were estimated from open
patient-level data and the others from the published tables of the study. Use the
catalogue below to find one for a domain, a study design or a teaching point. In
jamovi, all of them are in the scenario picker of *Simulated study* and *Compare
designs*, grouped by domain.

## How the scenarios were made

**From open data.** Many classic studies are distributed as datasets with R
packages (survival, MASS, datasets, HSAUR3, TH.data, pROC, medicaldata, aplore3,
NHANES). For each one the module's own [*Derive scenario*](derive.qmd) engine
estimated:

- the distribution of every baseline variable (normal, log-normal, gamma, counts,
  categories);
- their correlations, on a latent scale (a Gaussian copula);
- the conditional effects on the outcome, from the model the study would use
  (logistic, Cox, linear, Poisson or negative binomial).

When a study had few events for its number of variables, the effects were shrunk
towards no effect by one common factor, so the confounding between them is kept.

**From a published paper.** When no data are open, the parameters come from the
paper's tables: the baseline characteristics (Table 1), the frequency of the
outcome, and the adjusted estimates of the main analysis.

**Finishing by hand.** Data cannot tell causes from correlates, so each scenario
was then given:

- a causal structure (which variable affects which: confounders, mediators);
- reference categories and units;
- the designs that make sense for the question;
- labels and column names in English, Spanish and Catalan;
- a teaching note.

Variables that matter in the literature but had no effect in the data are kept as
*null variables*, useful for teaching multiple testing and confounding.

**Checking.** For every scenario and design, a large simulated study was analysed
as a student would analyse it. Its estimates were compared with the values the
data were generated with and with the source's main result. Examples:

- the alcohol odds ratios of the Ille-et-Vilaine study;
- the attenuated hazard ratio of local histology in the Wilms tumour study;
- the vaccine efficacy of the Salk trial;
- the AUC of high-sensitivity troponin.

**What a scenario is, and is not.** A scenario stores parameters, never the
original data. The data it produces resemble the source study in their
distributions, associations and main results, so analyses give the same
conclusions, but no row corresponds to a real person. The effect sizes are
teaching values that reproduce the source; they are not meta-analytic estimates,
and they should not be quoted as evidence. Every scenario lists its sources, and
the original investigators deserve the credit for the data.

## Catalogue

Filter by any column, or type in the search box (it searches names, populations,
outcomes and teaching notes). Click a column header to sort, and click a row for
its population, outcomes, teaching note and references.

```{r}
#| results: asis
cat(sprintf('<script id="cat-data" type="application/json">%s</script>', json))
```

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var data = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('cat-data').textContent);
  var el = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var arr = function (x) { return Array.isArray(x) ? x : (x == null ? [] : [x]); };
  var esc = function (s) { return String(s).replace(/[&<>"]/g, function (c) { return {'&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;'}[c]; }); };
  var uniq = function (f) { var s = {}; data.forEach(function (r) { arr(f(r)).forEach(function (v) { s[v] = 1; }); }); return Object.keys(s).sort(); };
  var fill = function (id, vals) { vals.forEach(function (v) { var o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = v; o.textContent = v; el(id).appendChild(o); }); };
  var designOrder = ['Cross-sectional', 'Cohort', 'Case-control', 'Matched case-control', 'Nested case-control', 'Case-cohort', 'Ecological',
                     'Randomised trial', 'Cluster trial', '2x2 factorial', 'Crossover', 'Longitudinal trial', 'Prognosis', 'Diagnostic accuracy'];
  fill('f-domain', uniq(function (r) { return r.domain; }));
  fill('f-design', designOrder.filter(function (d) { return data.some(function (r) { return arr(r.designs).indexOf(d) >= 0; }); }));
  fill('f-type', uniq(function (r) { return r.types; }));
  fill('f-source', uniq(function (r) { return r.source; }));
  fill('f-feature', uniq(function (r) { return r.features; }));

  // filters and sort survive a reload (per viewer, best effort)
  var state = { key: 'domain', dir: 1, open: {} };
  var save = function () { try { localStorage.setItem('studysim-cat', JSON.stringify({ f: ['f-text', 'f-domain', 'f-design', 'f-type', 'f-source', 'f-feature'].map(function (i) { return el(i).value; }), key: state.key, dir: state.dir })); } catch (e) {} };
  try { var s = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('studysim-cat') || 'null');
        if (s) { ['f-text', 'f-domain', 'f-design', 'f-type', 'f-source', 'f-feature'].forEach(function (i, k) { if (s.f && s.f[k] != null) el(i).value = s.f[k]; }); state.key = s.key || state.key; state.dir = s.dir || 1; } } catch (e) {}

  var matches = function (r) {
    var t = el('f-text').value.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (el('f-domain').value && r.domain !== el('f-domain').value) return false;
    if (el('f-design').value && arr(r.designs).indexOf(el('f-design').value) < 0) return false;
    if (el('f-type').value && arr(r.types).indexOf(el('f-type').value) < 0) return false;
    if (el('f-source').value && r.source !== el('f-source').value) return false;
    if (el('f-feature').value && arr(r.features).indexOf(el('f-feature').value) < 0) return false;
    if (t) {
      var hay = [r.id, r.label, r.domain, r.population, r.teaching, r.dataset].concat(arr(r.designs), arr(r.outcomes).map(function (o) { return o.label; }), arr(r.references)).join(' ').toLowerCase();
      return t.split(/\s+/).every(function (w) { return hay.indexOf(w) >= 0; });
    }
    return true;
  };
  var sortVal = function (r, k) { var v = r[k]; if (Array.isArray(v)) return v.join(', '); return typeof v === 'number' ? v : String(v || '').toLowerCase(); };

  var render = function () {
    var rows = data.filter(matches).sort(function (a, b) {
      var x = sortVal(a, state.key), y = sortVal(b, state.key);
      if (x < y) return -state.dir; if (x > y) return state.dir;
      return a.label < b.label ? -1 : 1;
    });
    var html = rows.map(function (r) {
      var open = state.open[r.id];
      var main = '<tr class="cat-row' + (open ? ' table-active' : '') + '" data-id="' + esc(r.id) + '" tabindex="0" aria-expanded="' + !!open + '">' +
        '<td><strong>' + esc(r.label) + '</strong><br><code class="small">' + esc(r.id) + '</code></td>' +
        '<td>' + esc(r.domain) + '</td>' +
        '<td>' + arr(r.designs).map(function (d) { return '<span class="badge rounded-pill border me-1 mb-1 fw-normal" style="color: inherit">' + esc(d) + '</span>'; }).join('') + '</td>' +
        '<td class="small">' + arr(r.types).map(esc).join(', ') + '</td>' +
        '<td class="small">' + esc(r.source) + '</td>' +
        '<td class="text-end">' + r.nvars + '</td></tr>';
      if (!open) return main;
      var det = '<tr class="cat-detail"><td colspan="6"><div class="p-2 small">' +
        '<p><strong>Population.</strong> ' + esc(r.population) + '</p>' +
        '<p><strong>Designs.</strong> ' + arr(r.designs).map(esc).join(', ') + '</p>' +
        '<p><strong>Outcomes.</strong> ' + arr(r.outcomes).map(function (o) { return esc(o.label) + ' (' + esc(o.type) + ')'; }).join('; ') + '</p>' +
        (arr(r.features).length ? '<p><strong>Features.</strong> ' + arr(r.features).map(esc).join(', ') + '</p>' : '') +
        '<p><strong>Teaching note.</strong> ' + esc(r.teaching) + '</p>' +
        (r.dataset ? '<p><strong>Data.</strong> ' + esc(r.dataset) + '</p>' : '') +
        '<p class="mb-0"><strong>Sources.</strong></p><ul class="mb-0">' + arr(r.references).map(function (x) { return '<li>' + esc(x) + '</li>'; }).join('') + '</ul>' +
        '</div></td></tr>';
      return main + det;
    }).join('');
    document.querySelector('#cat-table tbody').innerHTML = html || '<tr><td colspan="6" class="text-muted">No scenario matches these filters.</td></tr>';
    el('cat-count').textContent = rows.length + ' of ' + data.length + ' scenarios';
    document.querySelectorAll('#cat-table th').forEach(function (th) {
      th.textContent = th.textContent.replace(/ [▲▼]$/, '') + (th.getAttribute('data-k') === state.key ? (state.dir > 0 ? ' ▲' : ' ▼') : '');
      th.setAttribute('aria-sort', th.getAttribute('data-k') === state.key ? (state.dir > 0 ? 'ascending' : 'descending') : 'none');
    });
    var cov = el('cat-coverage');
    cov.innerHTML = designOrder.map(function (d) {
      var n = rows.filter(function (r) { return arr(r.designs).indexOf(d) >= 0; }).length;
      return '<button type="button" class="btn btn-sm ' + (el('f-design').value === d ? 'btn-primary' : 'btn-outline-secondary') + '" data-design="' + esc(d) + '"' + (n ? '' : ' disabled') + '>' +
             esc(d) + ' <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">' + n + '</span></button>';
    }).join('');
    save();
  };

  ['f-text', 'f-domain', 'f-design', 'f-type', 'f-source', 'f-feature'].forEach(function (i) { el(i).addEventListener('input', render); });
  el('f-reset').addEventListener('click', function () { ['f-text', 'f-domain', 'f-design', 'f-type', 'f-source', 'f-feature'].forEach(function (i) { el(i).value = ''; }); render(); });
  document.querySelectorAll('#cat-table th').forEach(function (th) {
    th.addEventListener('click', function () { var k = th.getAttribute('data-k'); state.dir = state.key === k ? -state.dir : 1; state.key = k; render(); });
  });
  var toggle = function (tr) { var id = tr.getAttribute('data-id'); state.open[id] = !state.open[id]; render(); };
  document.querySelector('#cat-table tbody').addEventListener('click', function (e) { var tr = e.target.closest('tr.cat-row'); if (tr) toggle(tr); });
  document.querySelector('#cat-table tbody').addEventListener('keydown', function (e) { var tr = e.target.closest('tr.cat-row'); if (tr && (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ')) { e.preventDefault(); toggle(tr); } });
  el('cat-coverage').addEventListener('click', function (e) { var b = e.target.closest('button[data-design]'); if (!b) return; var d = b.getAttribute('data-design'); el('f-design').value = el('f-design').value === d ? '' : d; render(); });
  render();
})();
</script>
```

## Choosing a scenario

- **For a design**, filter by design. Most scenarios fit several designs, and
  [*Compare designs*](simulated-study.qmd) simulates them from the same
  population: the classic contrasts are a case-control vs a cohort study for a
  rare cancer, an ecological vs an individual analysis (water hardness, dietary
  fat), or a parallel vs a crossover trial (hypnotics, asthma).
- **For a statistical idea**, use the features and the search box:
  - *confounding*: free light chains, lung cancer and smoking, NHANES;
  - *mediation*: myopia, birth weight;
  - *effect modification*: RECOVERY, ISIS-2, breast cancer risk;
  - *competing risks*: MGUS, PBC, colon cancer;
  - *misclassification*: Wilms tumour;
  - *overdispersion*: epilepsy;
  - *dropout*: Beat the Blues;
  - *overfitting with many markers*: glaucoma;
  - *rare outcomes and sample size*: polio vaccine.
- **For dentistry and podiatry courses**, filter the domains *Odontology*
  (periodontal treatment in pregnancy, fluoride varnish, periodontitis) and
  *Podiatry* (diabetic foot ulcer, onychomycosis, plantar fasciitis, ankle- and
  toe-brachial index).
- **For your own course**, export a scenario from *Library* as Excel or YAML,
  change it, and load it back; or derive a new one from your own data with
  [*Derive scenario*](derive.qmd).
